# Results — Study 651 (Sugar-Seasonality): does raw sugar (No.11) have a Brazil/India crush calendar? 2011–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly log returns of **CANE**, the
Teucrium Sugar Fund (a weighted roll across three ICE No.11 raw-sugar contract months — the
tradable, already-roll-costed instrument), built from daily adjusted closes resampled to
month-end, plus the roll-naive **SB=F** front-month futures splice used only as a spot-price
cross-check (never as something anyone could have earned). Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; CANE's 2011-09-19 inception sets the common start). Fingerprints `c0c35fdc0e66`
(CANE) / `88229d212e57` (SB=F).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes, CANE (Teucrium Sugar Fund) and SB=F (ICE No.11 roll-naive front-month futures), 2011-10-03 → 2026-06-30, resampled to **176 month-end observations per series** |
| Crush calendar | **hardcoded** table: Brazil Center-South cane crush (Apr–Nov), India cane-crushing season (Oct–Apr), and the claimed "pre-harvest tight" window (Jan–Mar) vs "crush-glut" window (Apr–Jul) — facts, no network; see `SUGAR_CALENDAR` / `TIGHT_MONTHS` / `CRUSH_MONTHS` in [`sugar_seasonality/data.py`](../sugar_seasonality/data.py) |
| Statistics | one-sample naive + **Newey-West (HAC)** *t* per calendar month (12 cells) with a **Bonferroni** bar for 12 simultaneous tests; Welch *t* for best/worst month vs rest and for tight-vs-crush; a circular block-bootstrap CI (5,000 draws, 12-month blocks) on the tight-minus-crush spread; Wilson interval on the seasonal timer's active-leg hit rate |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the calendar-known seasonal timer sets its position from the (fixed, published) crush calendar alone — no signal-to-trade lag is needed. Round-trip costs: 4 one-way legs/yr × 10 bps × NAV, spread across the 12 months |
| Roll caveat (named) | CANE is **not** a spot proxy — it holds a weighted roll across near/second/third ICE No.11 contract months and pays that roll's cost or benefit every month. SB=F is a roll-naive front-month splice: **not tradable as a continuous series**, used only to size CANE's own roll drag |

No survivorship on the Signal axis (a single continuously-listed ETF and a single continuous
futures ticker, not a cross-sectional panel).

## The headline — 12 calendar months, Bonferroni-corrected

Bonferroni bar for 12 simultaneous tests (α = 0.05/12, df≈13): **|t| ≥ 3.47**.

| Month | Mean | n | t (naive) | t (HAC) | Survives? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| Jan | +0.27% | 15 | +0.17 | +0.18 | No |
| Feb | +0.05% | 15 | +0.04 | +0.07 | No |
| Mar | −1.31% | 15 | −0.48 | −0.47 | No |
| Apr | −0.68% | 15 | −0.30 | −0.31 | No |
| May | **−2.11%** | 15 | −1.80 | −1.90 | No |
| Jun | +0.23% | 15 | +0.17 | +0.25 | No |
| Jul | −1.29% | 14 | −0.85 | −1.26 | No |
| Aug | −0.46% | 14 | −0.31 | −0.31 | No |
| Sep | **+1.44%** | 14 | +0.96 | +1.50 | No |
| Oct | −0.03% | 14 | −0.02 | −0.02 | No |
| Nov | −0.63% | 15 | −0.52 | −0.71 | No |
| Dec | −1.76% | 15 | −1.15 | −1.12 | No |

**Cells clearing the Bonferroni bar: 0/12.** No individual calendar month is a certified anomaly —
not one even clears the far weaker *nominal* |t| ≥ 2 line. The single largest-magnitude cell is May
(−2.11%, *t*<sub>HAC</sub> = −1.90) — inside the claimed crush-glut window and pointing the claimed
direction, but short of significance even before any multiple-testing penalty. The best month,
September (+1.44%, *t*<sub>HAC</sub> = +1.50), sits in the *back half* of Brazil's own crush window,
the opposite of "tight before the harvest."

## Best / worst calendar month vs the rest

| | Month | Mean | Welch *t* (vs rest) | n |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Best | Sep | +1.44% | +1.36 | 14 |
| Worst | May | −2.11% | −1.35 | 15 |

Neither the best nor the worst month clears |t| ≥ 2 against the rest of the calendar, let alone the
Bonferroni bar.

## Pre-harvest TIGHT (Jan–Mar) vs CRUSH-glut (Apr–Jul) — the decisive number

| | Mean monthly return | n |
|---|--:|--:|
| Tight (Jan–Mar, claimed high) | −0.33% | 45 |
| Crush (Apr–Jul, claimed low) | −0.96% | 59 |
| **Spread** | **+0.63%** | — |
| **Welch *t*** | **+0.46** | — |
| **Block-bootstrap 95% CI** | **[−1.89%, +2.98%]** | 5,000 resamples, 12-month blocks |

The spread points the claimed direction (tight *does* nominally beat crush) but is a rounding
error relative to its own uncertainty band — the CI is roughly six times wider than the point
estimate and straddles zero comfortably. **No certified pre-harvest-tight / crush-glut seasonal.**

## Third axis, part 1 — the ETF's own roll ("contango" caveat)

Mean monthly return, CANE (the tradable, roll-costed instrument) vs the roll-naive SB=F
front-month futures splice (spot-price proxy, not tradable as a continuous series), one-sample *t*
of the monthly gap.

| | CANE mean | SB=F splice mean | Drag (CANE − SB=F) | *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Sugar | −53.4 bps/mo | −33.3 bps/mo | **−20.1 bps/mo** | −0.80 | 176 |

CANE gives back a nominal **−20.1 bps/month (~−2.4%/yr)** to its own weighted roll relative to the
roll-naive front-month proxy — real, and in the direction that eats a long-side calendar bet, but
*not itself certified* (*t* = −0.80). Unlike study 648's WEAT, sugar's roll drag is not the
decisive blow here — the pooled seasonal itself is already indistinguishable from noise before any
roll cost is charged.

## Third axis, part 2 — the seasonal timer, gross/net, and does it beat a coin?

Long the tight window (Jan–Mar), short the crush window (Apr–Jul), cash otherwise (calendar-known
rule, no execution lag); costs 4 one-way legs/yr × 10 bps × NAV.

| | CAGR | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| Buy & hold CANE | −8.5% | −0.29 |
| Timer (gross) | +1.2% | +0.16 |
| Timer (net, 10 bps/leg) | +0.8% | +0.14 |

The timer's Sharpe *looks* like an improvement over buy-and-hold — but CANE has lost money on
average over this window (Sharpe −0.29 buy-and-hold), and the timer is flat (cash) for 5 of the 12
months every year, which mechanically de-levers a losing position. The direct test of "does the
active leg earn anything" is the hit rate:

| | Hit rate (active months only) | Wilson 95% | Mean per active month | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Timer active legs | **61/104 = 58.7%** | [49.0%, 67.6%] | +0.40% | **+0.60** |

**"Beats a coin?" — BUSTED.** The active-leg hit rate (58.7%) is nominally above 50%, but its
Wilson interval straddles 50% and the mean active-month return is statistically indistinguishable
from zero (*t* = 0.60 < 2). The apparent Sharpe gain over buy-and-hold is a cash-drag artifact of
sitting out an already-losing ETF half the year, not evidence of predictive skill.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic i.i.d. monthly-return world with a TUNABLE planted pre-harvest-tight-premium /
crush-discount pair; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (seasonal = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.23** (sd 1.01), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted seasonal = +12.0%/yr (seed 651) | **+4.73** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up decisively on a planted spread. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Tight-vs-crush spread **+0.63%/month, Welch *t* = +0.46**, block-bootstrap CI
  **[−1.89%, +2.98%]**. Zero of 12 calendar-month cells clear the Bonferroni bar (|t| ≥ 3.47); not
  one even clears the far weaker nominal |t| ≥ 2 line. The nominal direction is consistent with
  the folklore (tight > crush, worst month May sits inside the crush window) but every number is
  well within noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** CANE's own roll drags a nominal (uncertified, *t* = −0.80) −20.1
  bps/month against any long-tight bet; the seasonal timer's Sharpe "improvement" over buy-and-hold
  is a cash-drag artifact of sitting flat half the year on an ETF that has lost money on average —
  its active-leg hit rate is 58.7% (Wilson [49.0%, 67.6%]), not statistically better than a coin
  (*t* = 0.60).
- **"Beats a coin?" — BUSTED.** The seasonal timer's active months hit 58.7% of the time, but the
  Wilson interval straddles 50% and the mean per active month is statistically zero (*t* = 0.60) —
  not certifiably better than a fair coin.
